statements.t: We have also stopped development on ATA188, an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy targeting multiple sclerosis (MS).
Our T-cell immunotherapy platform is potentially applicable to a broad array of targets and diseases.
We will, at Pierre Fabre’s expense, continue to observe the regulatory activities and support Pierre Fabre in its efforts to obtain BLA approval.
In May 2025, we aligned with the FDA on a plan to address the issues raised by the FDA in the Response Letter and the path forward for resubmission of the tab-cel BLA at a Type A meeting.
On October 14, 2026, we announced that the FDA had accepted the resubmission for a Class 2 review and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act target action date of March 31, 2027.
As of September 30, 2026, our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $9.9 million, which we intend to use to fund our operations.

We expect that any revenue we generate from the A&R Commercialization Agreement, subject to the terms of the HCRx Agreement, will fluctuate from period to period as a result of the timing of potential milestone achievement and any potential regulatory approvals.
The risks and uncertainties associated with our research and development projects are discussed more fully in the section of this report titled “Item 1A.

We intend to file a new shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (2026 Registration Statement) to replace the 2023 Registration Statement following the filing of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q and before the 2023 Registration Statement expires on November 13, 2026.
If we do not file the 2026 Registration Statement before November 13, 2026, we will not be able to make sales under the 2023 ATM Facility until a new registration statement is declared effective.

If our public float remains below $75 million, the 2026 Registration Statement will be filed in reliance on General Instruction I.B.6 of Form S-3 and sales of our common stock under the 2026 Registration Statement, including at-the-market sales, will be limited to one-third of our public float, measured as of a date within 60 days prior to each sale, in any 12-month period, unless and until our public float…
We intend to continue to offer and sell shares of our common stock under the 2023 ATM Facility after the 2026 Registration Statement is declared effective.
Once the 2026 Registration Statement is declared effective, we will make no further sales under the 2023 Registration Statement.
We continue to incur significant research and development and other expenses related to our ongoing operations and expect to incur losses for the foreseeable future.

As a result, we will need additional capital to fund our operations, which we may raise through a combination of equity offerings, debt financings, other third party funding and other collaborations, strategic alliances and partnering arrangements.

In addition, we expect to continue to opportunistically seek access to additional funds through additional public or private equity offerings or debt financings including by utilizing the 2023 ATM Facility, through potential collaboration, partnering or other strategic arrangements, or a combination of the foregoing.

We will remain constrained by the limitations of General Instruction I.B.6 to Form S-3 until such time as our public float exceeds $75 million, at which time the number of securities we may sell under a Form S-3 registration statement will no longer be limited by the limitations of General Instruction I.B.6 to Form S-3.

Assuming our public float remains below $75 million, the 2026 Registration Statement will be subject to General Instruction I.B.6, which will limit the aggregate amount we may sell in primary offerings under that registration statement, including pursuant to the 2023 ATM Facility, in any 12-month period to one-third of our public float.
We do not know when, or if, we will generate sufficient revenue from commercialization to offset our operating expenses.

We anticipate that we will continue to generate losses for the foreseeable future, and we expect the accumulated losses to increase as we continue the development of, and seek regulatory approvals for, our product candidate.
We anticipate that we will need to raise substantial additional funding in the near term to finance our planned operations.

We expect to continue to seek access to additional funds through additional public or private equity offerings or debt financings, through potential collaboration, partnering or other strategic arrangements, or a combination of the foregoing.
We have based our projections of operating capital requirements on assumptions that may prove to be incorrect, and we may use all of our available capital resources sooner than we expect.
We expect to continue to seek access to the equity and debt capital markets to support our development efforts and operations.

As a result of economic conditions, general global economic uncertainty, political change and other factors, we do not know whether additional capital will be available when needed, or that, if available, we will be able to obtain additional capital on reasonable terms.

If we are unable to raise additional capital due to the volatile global financial markets, general economic uncertainty or other factors, we will be forced to delay, limit, reduce or terminate preclinical studies, clinical studies or other development activities for one or more of our product candidates.

to what extent we will generate revenues from the commercialization and sale of any of our product candidates that obtain regulatory approval
